meanings.usage: 指人的性情或情绪状态
描述带有负罪感的动作
指强烈地劝某人做某事
指把东西藏起来不让别人看到
指觉得有趣或好笑的状态
描述符合常规或标准的状态
指让人放松或平息情绪

examples.en: He decided to give up smoking last year.

phrases.usage: 镇定我的神经，使我放松

examples.en: She took a deep breath to calm her nerves.
examples.zh: 她深呼吸让自己放松下来。

phrases.usage: 继续做某事，坚持做某事

examples.en: They kept on offering me cigarettes.

phrases.usage: 超出我的承受能力，我无法忍受

examples.en: The pain was more than I could bear.
examples.zh: 疼痛超出了我的承受能力。

phrases.phrase: make no effort to do something
phrases.usage: 没有努力做某事，毫不费力做某事

examples.en: They made no effort to hide their amusement.
examples.zh: 他们毫不掩饰自己的笑意。

examples.en: He lit a cigarette to calm his nerves.
examples.zh: 他点了一根烟来镇定神经。

phrases.usage: 恢复正常，回到正常状态

examples.en: Things had returned to normal once more.
As Brian pointed out, it is the easiest thing.
examples.zh: 正如布莱恩指出的，这是最简单的事。

examples.en: I produced a packet of sweets from my pocket.
examples.zh: 我从口袋里掏出一包糖果。

phrases.phrase: the easiest thing in the world

examples.en: It is the easiest thing in the world to give up smoking.
examples.zh: 戒烟是世界上最容易的事。

grammar.title: 一般过去时与过去进行时
grammar.structure: When引导的时间状语从句中，从句用一般过去时，主句用过去进行时；或者主句用一般过去时，从句用过去进行时。
grammar.definition: 一般过去时描述在过去某个时间完成的动作；过去进行时描述在过去某个时间正在进行的动作。两者可以结合使用。 用于描述过去同时发生的动作，或一个动作发生时另一个动作正在进行。

examples.en: When my old friend Brian urged me to accept a cigarette, I took one.
examples.zh: 当我的老朋友布莱恩劝我接受一支烟时，我接了一支。

examples.en: While I was smoking, my wife was watching me.
examples.zh: 当我抽烟时，我的妻子正在看着我。

examples.en: After reading an article, I lit a cigarette.
examples.zh: 读完一篇文章后，我点了一根烟。

grammar.title: For + 时间段 + 过去时
grammar.structure: for + 一段时间 + 一般过去时
grammar.definition: 用for引出时间段，表示某个动作或状态持续了多长时间，常与过去时连用。 描述过去某事持续的时间长度，常与表示戒烟、等待等持续性动作连用。

examples.en: For a whole week I did not smoke at all.
examples.zh: 整整一周我一根烟都没抽。

examples.en: I stayed there for three hours.
examples.zh: 我在那里待了三个小时。

examples.en: She worked in London for five years.

grammar.title: too...to 和 more than + 情感动词
grammar.structure: too + adj/adv + (for someone) + to do something / more than + 情感动词(could/bear等)
grammar.definition: too + 形容词/副词 + to do something 表示太...以至于不能...；more than + 情感动词表示超过某种情感所能承受的程度。 用于强调某种程度超出承受范围，常用于表达无法忍受的情感。

examples.en: It was more than I could bear.
examples.zh: 这超出了我的承受能力。

examples.en: The box is too heavy to carry.
examples.zh: 这个箱子太重了，搬不动。

examples.en: She was too nervous to speak.
examples.zh: 她太紧张了，说不出话来。

patterns.pattern: For + 一段时间 + did not + 动词原形

original.en: For a whole week I did not smoke at all.
original.zh: 整整一周我一根烟都没抽。

imitations.en: For a month I did not drink coffee.
imitations.zh: 整整一个月我没喝咖啡。

imitations.en: For two hours he did not say a word.
imitations.zh: 整整两个小时他一句话都没说。

patterns.pattern: After + doing something, 主语 + 动词

original.en: After reading an article, I lit a cigarette.
original.zh: 读完一篇文章后，我点了一根烟。

imitations.en: After finishing my homework, I watched TV.
imitations.zh: 做完作业后，我看了电视。

imitations.en: After getting up, she made breakfast.

patterns.pattern: It is the easiest thing in the world to do something

original.en: It is the easiest thing in the world to give up smoking.
original.zh: 戒烟是世界上最容易的事。

imitations.en: It is the easiest thing in the world to learn English.
imitations.zh: 学英语是世界上最容易的事。

imitations.en: It is the hardest thing in the world to wake up early.
imitations.zh: 早起是世界上最难的事。

patterns.pattern: When + 一般过去时, 主语 + 过去时

original.en: When my old friend Brian urged me to accept a cigarette, it was more than I could bear.
original.zh: 当我的老朋友布莱恩劝我接受一支烟时，我无法忍受了。

imitations.en: When he offered me a drink, it was more than I could bear.
imitations.zh: 当他给我递饮料时，我忍不住了。

imitations.en: When she asked me to dance, I felt nervous.
imitations.zh: 当她邀请我跳舞时，我很紧张。

lines.en: After reading an article entitled 'Cigarette Smoking and Your Health' I lit a cigarette to calm my nerves .
lines.zh: 读完一篇题为《吸烟与健康》的文章之后，我点上了一枝香烟，来镇定一下自己紧张的神经。

lines.en: I smoked with concentration and pleasure as I was sure that this would be my last cigarette.
lines.zh: 我聚精会神而又愉快地吸着这枝烟。因为我确信这是我最后一枝烟了。

lines.en: For a whole week I did not smoke at all and during this time, my wife suffered terribly.
lines.zh: 整整一个星期我根本没有吸烟。

lines.en: I had all the usual symptoms of someone giving up smoking: a bad temper and an enormous appetite.
lines.zh: 在此期间，我妻子吃尽了苦头。

lines.en: My friends kept on offering me cigarettes and cigars.
lines.zh: 我具备了戒烟者通常表现出来的所有症状：脾气暴躁和食欲旺盛。

lines.en: They made no effort to hide their amusement whenever I produced a packet of sweets from my pocket.
lines.zh: 我的朋友们不断地向我递香烟和雪茄。

lines.en: After seven days of this I went to a party.
lines.zh: 每当我从口袋里掏出一包糖果时，他们都毫不掩饰地表现出他们对此感到非常好笑。

lines.en: Everybody around me was smoking and I felt extremely uncomfortable.
lines.zh: 这样过了7天以后，我去参加一次聚会。

lines.en: When my old friend Brian urged me to accept a cigarette, it was more than I could bear.
lines.zh: 我周围的每个人都在吸烟，我感到非常不自在。

lines.en: I took one guiltily, lit it and smoked with satisfaction.
lines.zh: 当我的老朋友布赖恩极力劝我接受一枝香烟时，我再也忍不住了。

lines.en: My wife was delighted that things had returned to normal once more.
lines.zh: 我内疚地接过一枝点上，心满意足地抽起来。

lines.en: Anyway, as Brian pointed out, it is the easiest thing in the world to give up smoking.
lines.zh: 一切又都恢复了正常，为此我妻子十分高兴。

lines.en: He himself has done it lots of times!
lines.zh: 不管怎么说，正如布赖恩指出的那样，戒烟是世界上最容易的事情，他自己就已戒了很多次了！

questions.q: For how long did the writer give up smoking?
questions.hint: 见 For a whole week I did not smoke at all 与 After seven days of this I went to a party。

questions.q: What symptoms did the writer have while giving up smoking?
questions.zh: 戒烟期间，作者出现了哪些症状？
questions.a: He had all the usual symptoms of someone giving up smoking: a bad temper and an enormous appetite.
questions.aZh: 他具备了戒烟者通常表现出来的全部症状：脾气暴躁和食欲旺盛。
questions.hint: 见 a bad temper and an enormous appetite。

questions.q: How did his friends react when he produced a packet of sweets from his pocket?
questions.zh: 当他从口袋里掏出一包糖果时，朋友们是什么反应？
questions.a: They made no effort to hide their amusement. Besides, they kept on offering him cigarettes and cigars.
questions.aZh: 他们毫不掩饰自己觉得好笑；此外还不断地向他递香烟和雪茄。
questions.hint: 见 made no effort to hide their amusement 与 kept on offering。

questions.q: Why did the writer finally take a cigarette at the party?
questions.zh: 聚会上，作者为什么最终还是接过了烟？
questions.a: Because everybody around him was smoking and he felt extremely uncomfortable; when his old friend Brian urged him to accept a cigarette, it was more than he could bear.
questions.aZh: 因为周围每个人都在吸烟，他感到极不自在；当老友布赖恩极力劝他接一枝烟时，他再也忍不住了。
questions.hint: 见 felt extremely uncomfortable 与 more than I could bear。

questions.q: Why was his wife delighted that things had returned to normal once more, and what is the joke behind the title?
questions.zh: 一切“恢复正常”，妻子为什么反而高兴？标题的笑点在哪儿？
questions.a: Because during his week without smoking she had suffered terribly from his bad temper and enormous appetite. The joke is that his 'last one' was never really the last, so the question mark in the title mocks his self-deception.
questions.aZh: 因为他戒烟那一周，妻子被他的坏脾气和大胃口折磨得吃尽苦头。笑点在于“最后一枝”从来不是真的最后一枝，标题的问号正是对他的嘲弄。
questions.hint: 综合 my wife suffered terribly 与标题的问号。

translation:
读完一篇题为《吸烟与健康》的文章之后，我点上了一枝香烟，来镇定一下自己紧张的神经。
我聚精会神而又愉快地吸着这枝烟。
因为我确信这是我最后一枝烟了。
整整一个星期我根本没有吸烟。
在此期间，我妻子吃尽了苦头。
我具备了戒烟者通常表现出来的所有症状：脾气暴躁和食欲旺盛。
我的朋友们不断地向我递香烟和雪茄。
每当我从口袋里掏出一包糖果时，他们都毫不掩饰地表现出他们对此感到非常好笑。
这样过了7天以后，我去参加一次聚会。
我周围的每个人都在吸烟，我感到非常不自在。
当我的老朋友布赖恩极力劝我接受一枝香烟时，我再也忍不住了。
我内疚地接过一枝点上，心满意足地抽起来。
一切又都恢复了正常，为此我妻子十分高兴。
不管怎么说，正如布赖恩指出的那样，戒烟是世界上最容易的事情，他自己就已戒了很多次了！
title: The last one?
subtitle: 最后一枝吗？

lead.question: 读完戒烟文章后，作者宣称那是最后一枝烟，他究竟戒了多久？
lead.warmup: 作者读完一篇题为《吸烟与健康》的文章，反而点上烟安抚紧张的神经，还自信地说这是“最后一枝”。他真的整整一周没抽烟，可脾气暴躁、食欲大增，妻子跟着吃尽苦头；朋友不断递烟，他只能靠糖果解馋。第七天的聚会上人人吞云吐雾，老友布赖恩一劝，他便内疚地接过一枝，七天努力就此作废。
goals: 复述作者从“最后一枝烟”到七天后再度破戒的幽默戒烟全过程
熟练运用 keep on doing、make no effort to do、more than one can bear、point out、after all
理解 it takes ... to do 与 it 作先行主语，以及 a 与 one 的区别
lead.summary: 本课以幽默笔调记录一次失败的戒烟：作者读完戒烟文章反而点烟镇定神经，发誓这是最后一枝，撑过七天却脾气暴躁、食欲大增，妻子吃尽苦头，最终在聚会上被老友一劝而破戒。语言重点：entitled 作后置定语；with + 抽象名词；keep on doing；it takes ... to do。
lead.tips: one 表数量、a 表类别：I took one = one cigarette，此处不可换成 a；entitled 是过去分词作后置定语。

exercises.q: 选词填空（calm / nerves / concentration / pleasure / satisfaction）：I lit a cigarette to ___① my ___②. I smoked with ___③ and ___④. At the party I took one guiltily and smoked with ___⑤.
汉译英（用 entitled、be sure of oneself）：读完一篇题为《吸烟与健康》的文章后，我点上一枝烟来镇定神经；当时我很自信，确信这将是我最后一枝烟。
exercises.a: After reading an article entitled 'Cigarette Smoking and Your Health', I lit a cigarette to calm my nerves; I was sure of myself at the time and believed that this would be my last cigarette.

exercises.q: 填空（suffer / symptom / temper / appetite / keep one's temper）：my wife ___① terribly. I had all the usual ___② of someone giving up smoking: a bad ___③ and an enormous ___④. With such a bad temper, it was hard for him to ___⑤.
exercises.a: suffered; symptoms; temper; appetite; keep his temper

exercises.q: 汉译英（用 keep on doing 与 make no effort to do）：我的朋友们不断地向我递香烟和雪茄；每当我从口袋里掏出一包糖果时，他们都毫不掩饰地表现出好笑。
exercises.a: My friends kept on offering me cigarettes and cigars. They made no effort to hide their amusement whenever I produced a packet of sweets from my pocket.

exercises.q: 汉译英（用 more than one can bear、urge）：当我的老朋友布赖恩极力劝我接一枝烟时，我再也忍不住了，内疚地低声答应了。
exercises.a: When my old friend Brian urged me to accept a cigarette, it was more than I could bear; I agreed in a low, guilty voice.

exercises.q: 用 a 或 one 填空：① I lit ___ cigarette to calm my nerves. ② I took ___ guiltily, lit it and smoked with satisfaction. ③ He has given up smoking ___ hundred times.
exercises.note: a 表类别，one 表数量。

exercises.q: 汉译英（用 after all、it takes ... to do、point out、delighted）：毕竟，戒烟需要极大的毅力；可正如布赖恩指出的那样，戒烟又是世界上最容易的事情。一切恢复正常，我妻子似乎十分高兴。
exercises.a: After all, it takes great determination to give up smoking; but, as Brian pointed out, it is the easiest thing in the world to give up smoking. My wife seemed delighted that things had returned to normal once more.
exercises.note: it takes...to do；it 先行主语。

After reading an article entitling 'Cigarette Smoking and Your Health'
After reading an article which entitling 'Cigarette Smoking and Your Health'
After reading an article was entitled 'Cigarette Smoking and Your Health'

options: I lit a cigarette to calm my nerves.
I lit a cigarette to calm my nerve.
I lit a cigarette to quiet my nerve.
I lit a cigarette for calm my nerves.

options: They made no effort to hide their amusement.
They made no efforts hiding their amusement.
They made not effort to hide their amusement.
They made no effort hiding their amusement.
It was more than I could bear.
It was more than I could bare.
It was much more than I can bear.
It was more than I could bearing.
I took one guiltily.
I took a guiltily.
I took one of guiltily.

options: As Brian pointed out, it is the easiest thing in the world to give up smoking.
As Brian pointed out, that is the easiest thing in the world to give up smoking.
As Brian pointed, it is the easiest thing in the world to give up smoking.
As Brian pointed out, it is the easiest thing in the world giving up smoking.
